title: Usha Devi (Smt.) v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
disposition: Writ petition allowed; District Magistrate's order ceasing the petitioner's financial/administrative powers as Gram Pradhan quashed
headnote: Not an electricity/Supply Code case — a U.P. Panchayat Raj Act ruling on the preliminary/fact-finding enquiry procedure required under the proviso to Section 95(1)(g) before a District Magistrate may cease a Gram Pradhan's financial and administrative powers pending a removal proceeding, applying the Full Bench decision in Vivekanand Yadav v. State of U.P. Recorded compactly given its complete absence of electricity/Supply Code nexus (it concerns village-panchayat governance and Rules, 1997 enquiry-officer qualifications); noted in this corpus's master citation ledger only because the case was collected among search results for Supply Code-adjacent material.

holding_units.code: U.P. Panchayat Raj Act, 1947 (s.95(1)(g) and proviso) read with U.P. Panchayat Raj (Removal of Pradhans, Up-Pradhans and Members) Enquiry Rules, 1997
holding_units.clause: Proviso to s.95(1)(g) — preliminary/fact-finding enquiry must be conducted by a person qualifying as 'Enquiry Officer' under Rule 2(c) of the 1997 Rules, or by the District Magistrate himself, before financial/administrative powers may be ceased
holding_units.topic: A report submitted by an officer not validly appointed as 'Enquiry Officer' under Rule 2(c) of the 1997 Rules (and not a District-Level Officer) cannot constitute a valid preliminary enquiry report for ceasing a Gram Pradhan's financial and administrative powers under the proviso to s.95(1)(g)
holding_units.holding: The District Magistrate's order was quashed. Applying the Full Bench ruling in Vivekanand Yadav v. State of U.P., a valid preliminary enquiry report for purposes of ceasing a Pradhan's powers under the proviso to s.95(1)(g) must be submitted either by the District Magistrate himself or by a person appointed and qualifying as 'Enquiry Officer' under Rule 2(c) of the 1997 Rules (ordinarily a District-Level Officer). Here, the officer (Assistant Director, Savings) who submitted the report relied upon by the District Magistrate was never validly appointed as Enquiry Officer (the only such appointment, of the District Savings Officer, never resulted in a submitted report) and did not, in any event, qualify as a District-Level Officer under Rule 2(c); his report was accordingly not a valid basis for the impugned order.
holding_units.limiting_facts: The petitioner, an elected Gram Pradhan, was restrained from exercising financial/administrative powers on the basis of a report by the Assistant Director (Savings), Jaunpur, alleging misappropriation of Rs. 7,97,744 in panchayat construction funds; the District Magistrate's actual enquiry-officer appointment (District Savings Officer) never submitted the relied-upon report.
holding_units.flag: Recorded compactly given its complete absence of electricity/Supply Code nexus; not exhaustively digested against this corpus's doctrinal framework.

authorities.name: Vivekanand Yadav v. State of U.P. & Anr.
authorities.proposition: Sets out the complete procedural framework for preliminary/fact-finding enquiry and final removal enquiry under s.95(1)(g) of the U.P. Panchayat Raj Act, 1947 and the 1997 Enquiry Rules, including who qualifies as 'Enquiry Officer'.
